note: Example exports for the 28 draft experiments.

datasets.acquisition_path: phyphox audio input, 48 kHz, 0.1 s analysis blocks
datasets.scenario: Motor-off and motor-on plateaus, with 0.1 s block RMS values.
realism: 48 kHz sample rate and 4800 samples per 0.1 s block.
Relative digital amplitude, not calibrated or A-weighted sound pressure.
10 dB motor-on level change with block-to-block variation.
Raw audio samples are omitted because the full 48 kHz stream is large; the block table is the analysis record.

datasets.scenario: Stationary phone beside a small motor switched on for three 10 s intervals.
realism: Earth field near 48 µT plus a motor-dependent vector of a few µT.
0.15 µT broadband noise and a small 5 Hz motor ripple.
Accuracy code 3 is reported as a high-confidence phone magnetometer sample.

datasets.scenario: Flat, ±20° tilts, a short shake, a 60° roll, and a return to flat.
realism: ±2 g, 8-bit KXTJ9 setting with 64 counts per g.
Signed int8 counts, including the -128 minimum byte.
Bias of 0.20, -0.25, 0.35 m/s² and 0.02 m/s² noise.
10 Hz receive-time stream; the 100 ms request is not a guaranteed conversion clock.

datasets.acquisition_path: SensorTag AA51 notification, 100 ms assumed period
datasets.scenario: Stationary, ±125 °/s yaw, ±200 °/s roll/pitch, then stationary again.
realism: 500 °/s total span and 500/65536 °/s per signed count.
Small zero-rate bias in rad/s and 0.8 °/s rate noise.
Signed little-endian 16-bit packet components.
Receive time is a phone clock, not a device conversion time.

datasets.acquisition_path: SensorTag AA21 notification, 1 s assumed period
datasets.scenario: Slow warming with a short humidity breath event near 30 s.
realism: SHT21 equations RH = 125 SRH/65536 - 6 and T = 175.72 ST/65536 - 46.85.
Low two status bits set and masked before conversion.
0.05 °C and 0.4 %RH noise; outside-domain RH becomes nan.
One receive clock shared by the paired temperature and humidity words.

datasets.sensor: TI CC2541 SensorTag TMP006 infrared thermopile
datasets.acquisition_path: SensorTag AA01 notification, 1 s assumed period
datasets.scenario: A warm target is held near 35 °C and 45 °C, then cools, while the die warms slightly.
realism: 156.25 nV per thermopile count and 1/128 °C per die count.
Signed voltage and die words, including negative voltage counts.
Application model coefficients are example calibration values, not a certificate.
Object output is the TMP006 compensated fourth-root result.

datasets.scenario: Earth-field baseline, 80° yaw, 20° tilt, a magnet approach near 43 s, then return.
realism: MAG3110 nominal 0.1 µT per signed count and 10 Hz period request.
Bias of 5, -3, 8 µT and 0.12 µT noise.
Hard-iron offset and a magnet disturbance are retained as sensor-frame components.
The scale-verified gate is assumed enabled for this example.

datasets.scenario: A near-ambient baseline, a +20 hPa chamber excursion, a small leak, and release.
realism: T5400 compensation polynomial with the fixture calibration coefficients.
Signed UT and unsigned UP 16-bit words.
1 Hz polling timestamps receipt of the data read, not the conversion instant.
Calibration is assumed loaded and verified for this example.

datasets.sensor: Arduino Nano 33 BLE Sense APDS-9960 RGBC
datasets.scenario: Warm 2700 K, neutral 4000 K, cool 6500 K, and warm again, each held for 10–15 s.
realism: Raw RGBC counts with APDS channel gains and 4100-count clamping.
The documented donor XYZ matrix and McCamy polynomial are applied.
The accepted CCT is gated to the 2000–10000 K screening interval.
Broad-band RGBC cannot establish a full spectrum or a stellar temperature.

datasets.sensor: Fixed-exposure camera and external ROI analysis
datasets.acquisition_path: Manual image-region statistics, two repeats per mask/separation
datasets.scenario: Six image separations from 30 to 180 px, each with mask absent and present.
realism: Target and background ROI means in arbitrary linear image units.
A 10 ms fixed exposure and a 255-unit unsaturated ceiling.
Masked images reduce both target and background, as a real occulting disk would.
Contrast is local (target minus background)/background, not a planet/star flux ratio.

datasets.scenario: Dark, stable 1000-count baseline, then 1%, 2%, 4%, and 8% light features.
realism: APDS counts with channel gains and 4100-count clamping.
The feature depths are relative to the illuminated baseline.
Device and phone receive clocks are both present and not identical.
The summary row reports delivered rates and baseline noise, not chip bandwidth.

datasets.acquisition_path: Derived summary from the 20 Hz example record
datasets.scenario: Summary of the measured intervals and 12–28 s baseline.
realism: Intervals are computed from the actual example timestamps.
Baseline mean and sample standard deviation use the selected window.
The SNR is a planning quantity for a 2% drop, not a detection claim.

datasets.scenario: Alternating 30% primary and 10% secondary minima with a 30 s primary-to-primary period.
realism: Raw clear/RGB counts with APDS gains and noise.
Normalized light uses dark 10 counts and baseline 210 counts.
Phase uses epoch 20 s and period 30 s.
Primary and secondary labels are observationally defined, not an orbital fit.

datasets.scenario: Baseline, planet-only, separated moon, overlapping moon, separated moon, planet-only, baseline.
realism: Counts follow the intended ordering baseline ≥ planet-only ≥ overlap ≥ separated ≥ dark.
Normalized light uses dark 10 and baseline 110 counts.
The overlap interval is a local brightening relative to the separated interval.
The example does not assign a moon radius or a barycentric orbit.

datasets.sensor: TI SensorTag CC2650/CC1350 BMP280 die temperature
datasets.scenario: Lamp off for 60 s, on for 180 s, then off again; the die warms by about 8 K.
realism: BMP280 signed 24-bit temperature word with 0.01 °C scaling.
Baseline 22 °C, +0.7 °C self-heating, and 0.02 °C noise.
Receive time is used directly, not reconstructed from sample count.
Die temperature is a device proxy, not isolated gas temperature.

datasets.scenario: Six ruler positions from 0.20 to 0.70 m, with settles between moves.
realism: Raw APDS counts and both device and receive clocks.
Clear signal follows 1/r² with a 10-count background.
RGB counts track the same lamp spectrum.
The paired observation table is a separate example file.

datasets.sensor: Arduino Nano 33 BLE Sense APDS-9960 and manual ruler
datasets.acquisition_path: Recorded snapshots from the 20 Hz light stream
columns: Corrected signal times distance squared (count m²)
datasets.scenario: Twelve settled ruler observations, forward and back.
realism: Each row captures the latest light sample and its two timestamps.
Background 10 counts and positive-distance gates are applied.
The corrected signal times distance squared is nearly constant.
No interpolation between manual positions is implied.

columns: Previous mouse displacement at light time (counts)
Corrected illuminance times distance squared (lx m²)
datasets.scenario: Lamp-off background 2 lx and a 1/r² illuminance sweep from 0.20 to 0.80 m.
realism: Exact OPT3001 exponent/mantissa encoding and 3% gain error.
1% optical noise and a 2 lx background.
At each light time the most recent previous mouse sample supplies the distance.
Mouse and light receive clocks are separate.

datasets.scenario: Carriage moves outward from 0.20 to 0.80 m and back in 0.05–0.10 m steps.
realism: 0.0002 m per count and a 0.15 m reset-origin distance.
Signed dx/dy reports integrated into x and y.
Small tracking noise and a straight rail; no arbitrary 2-D path.
Mouse and light clocks are independent.

datasets.scenario: DC current steps 0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, 0.2, and 0 A, each held for 8 s.
realism: Bz = 30 µT + 50 µT/A × current with 0.35 µT noise.
Two-point calibration B1=30 µT at 0 A and B2=50 µT at 0.4 A.
Accuracy code 3 is reported; DC plateaus only.
Geometry and nearby magnetic background are assumed fixed.

datasets.scenario: Analyzer angle stepped from 0° to 90° in 10° increments, with settles.
realism: Clear counts follow 10 + 1000 cos²(theta).
APDS channel gains, noise, and 4100-count clipping.
The angle is a manual protractor observation, not a gyro measurement.
The paired observation table is a separate example file.

datasets.sensor: Arduino Nano 33 BLE Sense APDS-9960 and manual protractor
datasets.acquisition_path: Recorded settled angle snapshots from the 20 Hz light stream
datasets.scenario: Ten angle observations with an aligned parallel axis and a 10-count floor.
realism: Cos-squared prediction with an angle zero of 0°.
Normalized transmission uses background 10 and parallel signal 1010 counts.
Small residuals reflect count noise and angle settling.
The table does not acquire the Nano gyroscope simultaneously.

datasets.scenario: Three 4% transits of 4 s duration at 20, 50, and 80 s.
realism: Clear/RGB counts with APDS gains, noise, and 4100-count clipping.
Normalized light uses dark 10 and baseline 110 counts.
A 4 s event spans about 80 samples at 20 Hz.
Threshold timing and projected radius remain analysis results, not columns here.

datasets.scenario: Stationary, ±500 °/s yaw, +250/−250 °/s roll, then stationary.
realism: 2000/32768 °/s per signed big-endian count.
Gyro x at byte 8, y at byte 6, z at byte 10.
Bias of 0.01, -0.02, 0.015 rad/s and 1.5 °/s rate noise.
Receive time is a phone clock; no device timestamp is present.

datasets.sensor: Calibrated absolute-pressure instrument and liquid-temperature probe
columns: Observation code (0 liquid, 1 sustained boiling, 2 uncertain)
datasets.scenario: Fifteen settled pressure/temperature pairs from 101.3 kPa down to 5 kPa, with liquid, boiling, and uncertain codes.
realism: Saturation temperatures follow the Antoine water curve.
Pressure uncertainty 0.1 kPa and temperature uncertainty 0.2 K.
Boiling code 1 is an operator judgement, not an automatic phase-boundary detection.
The table is a classroom observation map, not a complete phase diagram.

datasets.acquisition_path: Puck.js Nordic UART notification, 4 Hz timer
datasets.scenario: Dark, open reference, sample, open reference, dark intervals.
realism: Puck.light() is a relative 0..1 response, not lux.
4 Hz sampling with independent device and receive clocks.
0.02 noise and a 0.02 dark / 0.90 reference calibration.
The ratio is gated by the reference validity in the experiment.

datasets.scenario: Dark, unfiltered reference, red, green, blue filters, reference, dark.
realism: Raw APDS counts with channel gains, noise, and 4100-count clipping.
Transmission = (S−D)/(R−D) per channel with same-geometry references.
Filter plateaus are not spectra and are not calibrated lux.
The count ceiling is a screening bound, not a measured linearity limit.

datasets.scenario: Twelve 5 s plateaus: upright or tilted axis, two orbital positions, three latitudes.
realism: Clear counts follow a cosine-like illumination proxy.
Raw RGBC counts include APDS gains, noise, and clipping.
Labels are manual operator entries, not electronic geometry.
The observation table is a separate example file.

datasets.sensor: Arduino Nano 33 BLE Sense APDS-9960 and manual labels
datasets.acquisition_path: Recorded observation rows from the 20 Hz light stream
datasets.scenario: Twelve labeled observations covering trial, latitude, orbit position, and obliquity.
realism: Source distance is fixed at 100 cm for all rows.
Dark 10 counts and baseline 1100 counts are stored per row.
Relative response is a detector comparison, not a temperature ratio.
Labels and positions are manual, not electronic measurements.

datasets.scenario: Near-ambient pressure and a slowly warming barometer die.
realism: Pressure and die temperature words are scaled by 0.01.
0.02 hPa and 0.02 °C noise.
Barometer receive times are offset from the humidity stream.
No interpolation or common clock is implied.

datasets.scenario: Slow warming and a humidity pulse from 30 to 80 s.
realism: HDC1000 conversions T = 165 raw/65536 − 40 and RH = 100 raw/65536.
Low two humidity status bits set and masked.
0.05 °C and 0.4 %RH noise; no condensation correction.
Humidity and barometer notifications keep separate receive clocks.

datasets.sensor: Calibrated spectrometer or calibrated spectrum files
datasets.scenario: Twenty-one 15 nm bins from 400 to 700 nm with stellar and sample absorption features.
realism: All four intensities are in the same linear arbitrary units.
Reference exceeds dark; sample and star remain below the 200-unit ceiling.
A 589 nm comparison line is used below 622 nm and 656 nm above.
Line depths are relative to the entered continuum, not a molecular retrieval.

datasets.scenario: Normal transits at 20 and 80 s; an adjacent plateau at 45–49/55–59 s; a spot crossing at 50–54 s.
realism: Raw APDS counts with channel gains and noise.
Normalized light uses dark 10 and patched baseline 110 counts.
The spot crossing is an upward anomaly relative to the adjacent plateau.
No spot radius, temperature, or unique stellar map is inferred.

datasets.scenario: Ramp held at 0° for 5 s, raised to 25° by 20 s, then held while slip begins.
realism: Gravity vector in phone coordinates with 0.02 m/s² noise.
Inclination from atan2(hypot(gx,gy), abs(gz)).
The mount is assumed parallel to the contact plane.
The capture summary is analysis output, not a per-sample column here.

datasets.scenario: Stationary noise, a 0.5 s 2 m/s² slip excursion at 20 s, then 0.8 m/s² motion.
realism: Absolute linear acceleration in m/s².
Baseline noise about 0.1 m/s².
The slip threshold is a detection setting, not a calibrated material constant.
Gravity and linear acceleration retain separate clocks.

datasets.sensor: External UV detector on Nano A0
datasets.acquisition_path: Recorded observations from the 20 Hz analog stream
datasets.scenario: Six observations with sample counts 310, 250, 180, 310, 250, 310.
realism: ADC gain 3.3 V / 1023 counts and zero offset.
Detector irradiance gain 0.01 W/m²/V as an example calibration.
Transmission is a detector-weighted band ratio, not a resolved UV spectrum.
All voltage values stay inside the 0–3.3 V input range.

datasets.sensor: External UV detector on Nano A0
datasets.scenario: Dark, unfiltered reference, UV sample, reference, dark.
realism: 10-bit ADC counts 0–1023 with the default firmware resolution.
A0 dark 10 counts, reference 610 counts, sample 310 counts.
A1 and A2 carry only noise in this example.
The APDS RGB sensor is not used as a UV detector.
